message.content:
You are reviewing a code diff for REUSE issues only: new code that reimplements something the codebase already has. Do not look for correctness bugs.

Context: this is a small diff from an "andesim" hybrid RISC-V simulator project. It fixes a real bug (a nonexistent `--kanata-roi` flag was being sent to a subprocess called vsim, causing every hybrid `--kanata` pipeline-trace run to fail) and extends a ROI-marking mechanism in llama.cpp's ggml library to bracket N consecutive matrix-multiply operations instead of just 1.

Two repos:
1. `/home/nick/work/andesim` — diff at `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619/scratchpad/simplify2_andesim.diff` (driver/hybrid.cpp, driver/hybrid.hpp, driver/hybrid_test.cpp, tests/e2e.sh, plus doc updates in ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md and docs/llama_roi_howto.md — the doc files are prose, skip those for this review, focus on the code files)
2. `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` — diff at `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619/scratchpad/simplify2_llamacpp.diff` (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c — note this diff shows the WHOLE ROI-marker mechanism as new since it was never committed before; only the K+N-1 range-tracking arithmetic is actually new work from this latest round, the single-K version predates it, but review whatever is in the diff)

Read both diff files in full (they're small, well under 300 lines combined). For each file, check:
- `driver/hybrid.cpp`/`hybrid_test.cpp`: the fix just removes one line (`out.push_back("--kanata-roi");`). Confirm there's nothing else in this area that reimplements existing driver argv-building patterns rather than reusing them (grep `driver/` for similar "build a vector<string> of forwarded flags" helpers if any exist).
- `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`: the new `andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K + ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N - 1` range-end check — is this a standard/obvious range-membership pattern, or does it duplicate some existing range-check idiom already used elsewhere in this same dispatch function or file that should have been reused instead?
- `tests/e2e.sh`: the fix just drops `--kanata-roi` from an array append. Confirm nothing else needed changing.

Report only real findings with file, line, a one-line summary, and the existing helper/pattern being duplicated. If you find nothing significant (plausible, given the diff is mostly a one-line deletion plus a small counter-comparison), say so plainly and don't manufacture findings. Keep the report under 250 words.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.

Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */
